32190-the-works-of-alexander-pope-volume.creator: Unknown
32190-the-works-of-alexander-pope-volume.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The volume of 1735 contains, with a few exceptions, the poems which Pope had printed since 1717. The pages of each group of pieces--Epistles, Satires, Epitaphs, etc.--are numbered separately, and there are other irregularities in the numbers, arising from a change in the order of the Moral Essays after the sheets were struck off.

43958-minnewaska-mountain-houses.title: Minnewaska Mountain Houses
43958-minnewaska-mountain-houses.creator: Unknown
43958-minnewaska-mountain-houses.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Still nearer, in a deep glen of the mountain, is the Palmaghatt, where is a large forest of massive primeval hemlocks. To all these and many other strange and picturesque places, good walks have been constructed, and a large number of covered seats and summer-houses (about ninety in all) have been built. Three drives have been built recently to Millbrook Mountains, Kempton Ledge, and Beacon Hill.

Many of these were used by Sir WALTER SCOTT in the compilation of the Minstrelsy of the Scottish Border; many, again, not less important than the others, did not find a place in that collection.

arxiv-2103-15473.title: Determination of paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases of an Ising model on a third-order Cayley tree
arxiv-2103-15473.creator: H. Akın
arxiv-2103-15473.description: Abstract In this present paper, the recurrence equations of an Ising model with three coupling constants on a third-order Cayley tree are obtained. Paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases associated with the Ising model are characterized. Types of phases and partition functions corresponding to the model are rigorously studied.

arxiv-2111-05824.title: Very weak solution for the exterior stationary Stokes equations with Navier slip boundary condition
arxiv-2111-05824.creator: Anis Dhifaoui
arxiv-2111-05824.description: Abstract In some problems of fluid mechanics, it is possible to be confronted with data that are not regular, that is why we are interested here in the search for the so-called very weak solutions for the stationary Stokes problem with Navier-type boundary conditions in a three-dimensional exterior domain.

arxiv-2212-06766.title: Homomorphism Conjugacy versus Centralizer Actions in the Symmetric Group
arxiv-2212-06766.creator: Suleika Norrbom
arxiv-2212-06766.description: Abstract We explore when generator-conjugate homomorphisms are conjugate and when element-conjugate homomorphisms are conjugate from abelian or dihedral groups to the symmetric group. We completely determine when such homomorphisms are conjugate in the case where the source group has two generators by studying centralizer actions in the target group.

arxiv-2301-01890.title: Modular Mix-and-Match Complementation of Büchi Automata (Technical Report)
arxiv-2301-01890.creator: Vojtěch Havlena, Ondřej Lengál, Yong Li, Barbora Šmahlíková, Andrea Turrini
arxiv-2301-01890.description: Abstract Complementation of nondeterministic Büchi automata (BAs) is an important problem in automata theory with numerous applications in formal verification, such as termination analysis of programs, model checking, or in decision procedures of some logics. We build on ideas from a recent work on BA determinization by Li et al. and propose a new modular algorithm for BA complementation.

arxiv-2309-15389.title: Quantum particle under dynamical confinement: From quantum Fermi acceleration to high harmonic generation
arxiv-2309-15389.creator: S. Rakhmanov, C. Trunk, D. Matrasulov
arxiv-2309-15389.description: Abstract Quantum dynamics of a particle confined in a box with time-dependent wall is revisited by considering some unexplored aspects of the problem. In particular, the case of dynamical confinement in a time-dependent box in the presence of purely time-varying external potential is treated by obtaining exact solution.

arxiv-2405-14415.title: Progress in implementing the kinematical constraint into the small-x JIMWLK evolution equation
arxiv-2405-14415.creator: P. Korcyl, L. Motyka and T. Stebel
arxiv-2405-14415.description: Abstract The most complete high-energy evolution of Wilson line operators is described by the set of equations called Balitsky-JIMWLK evolution equations. It is known from the studies of the linear - the BFKL - evolution equation that the leading corrections come from the kinematically enhanced double collinear logarithms.

arxiv-2501-09153.title: Layered Dirichlet Modeling to Assess the Changing Contributions of MLB Players as they Age
arxiv-2501-09153.creator: Monnie McGee, Jacob Turner, Bianca Luedeker
arxiv-2501-09153.description: Abstract Abstract The productive career of a professional athlete is limited compared to the normal human lifespan. Most professional athletes have retired by age 40. The early retirement age is due to a combination of age-related performance and life considerations.

pmc-11525250.title: A hierarchical reinforcement learning model explains individual differences in attentional set shifting
pmc-11525250.creator: Anahita Talwar, Francesca Cormack, Quentin J M Huys, Jonathan P Roiser
pmc-11525250.description: Attentional set shifting refers to the ease with which the focus of attention is directed and switched. Cognitive tasks, such as the widely used CANTAB IED, reveal great variation in set shifting ability in the general population, with notable impairments in those with psychiatric diagnoses.

pmc-11641316.title: How Mental Health Nurses Perceive the Implementation of Batho Pele Principles in a Selected Mental Health Hospital in Limpopo Province, South Africa
pmc-11641316.creator: Nkhensani Florence Mabunda
pmc-11641316.description: Background: Batho Pele is a South African legislative framework initiative introduced to improve the overall delivery of public services. The framework was introduced in 1997 and aimed at bringing a comprehensive transformation of the work ethics of all public servants, including health workers, at all levels of health hospitals.

pmc-11657782.title: Blood biomarkers to detect functional impairment in adult patients with repaired tetralogy of Fallot
pmc-11657782.creator: S. Alborikan, A. Althunayyan, B. Pandya, K. Von Klemperer, F. Walker, S. Cullen, A. Bhan, S. Badiani, D. Encarnacion, R. Monteiro, S.E. Petersen, S. Bhattacharyya, G. Lloyd
pmc-11657782.description: BackgroundThe relationship between plasma brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and soluble suppression of tumorigenicity-2 (sST2) with structural adaptions and exercise capacity remains incompletely described in patients with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF).MethodsPeripheral venous blood samples were drawn for 99 patients with repaired TOF, 59 patients with severe pulmonary regurgitation (PR) and 40 patients with no or mild PR.

pmc-12640947.title: The transcriptional and cellular landscape of cognitive resilience to Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-12640947.creator: Nina Khera, Ravikiran M. Raju, Stuart A. Lipton
pmc-12640947.description: It is estimated that 5%–40% of patients with pathological features of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) maintain normal cognitive health throughout their lifetimes, a phenomenon known as cognitive resilience. Studies have identified many factors that contribute to a patient’s capacity for resilience, with those that modulate gene expression being the most dynamic, adaptable, and potentially addressable as targets for future drug development.

pmc-12653697.title: Native Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungal Communities in Trap Cultures Are Shaped by Traditional Host Plants and Agricultural Soils
pmc-12653697.creator: Michael Sakha, Joseph P. Gweyi-Onyango, Manoj Kaushal, Frederick P. Baijukya, Cargele Masso
pmc-12653697.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi inoculants are increasingly recognized as effective biofertilizers in sustainable agriculture. Typically, as a first step for AM fungi inoculum production, a trap culture system using mycotrophic host plants is commonly used to isolate AM fungi. However, the influence of traditional host plants and agricultural field soil on the composition of AM fungal communities in trap cultures remains poorly understood.

pmc-12732963.creator: María Virginia Matulič Domandzič, José Manuel Díaz González, Núria Fustier García, Eliana González Gómez
pmc-12732963.description: Highlights Public health relevance—How does this work relate to a public health issue? Homeless women face compounded health vulnerabilities due to gender-based violence, chronic illness, and mental health conditions that remain largely unaddressed.Barriers in access to healthcare deepen health inequities for a population already experiencing extreme forms of social exclusion.

pmc-12735548.title: First In Vitro Human Islet Assessment of Oleanolic Acid (OA) and Its Serine Conjugate: Enhanced Solubility with Comparable Effects
pmc-12735548.creator: Runkai Yin, Li Zhao, Lina A Huang, Rui Zhao, Andy Wu, Maggie Rao, Jason Wu, Claire Wu, Fouad R Kandeel, Junfeng Li, Antonio Palumbo Piccionello
pmc-12735548.description: Oleanolic acid (OA) is a natural pentacyclic triterpenoid with reported hypoglycemic, hepatoprotective, antidiabetic, and anti-inflammatory activities. However, its limited aqueous solubility restricts its formulation and potential biomedical applications. To address this limitation, we designed a hydrophilic OA derivative, 1a, by introducing an amino acid fragment at the C-28 position.

pmc-13038640.title: Can Evidential Pluralism mitigate bias and motivated reasoning?
pmc-13038640.creator: Joe Jones, Alexandra Trofimov, Michael Wilde, Jon Williamson
pmc-13038640.description: This paper defends Evidential Pluralism, a philosophical account of causal enquiry, against the concern that it is particularly prone to bias and motivated reasoning. Evidential Pluralism scrutinises mechanistic studies alongside the comparative studies considered by the evaluation methods at the heart of orthodox evidence-based medicine and evidence-based policy.
